scenes.title: The Case Against Tragedy
scenes.summary: Tragedy, it is said, is vulgar: its performers overact, as Mynniscus called Callippides an ape, while epic is for decent audiences.

scenes.title: The Fault Is the Actors'
scenes.summary: The charge is against acting, not poetry: rhapsodes too overdo it, not all movement is bad, and tragedy does its work even when read.

scenes.title: Why Tragedy Is Higher
scenes.summary: Tragedy has everything epic has and music besides, vividness in reading and in performance, concentration, and greater unity; so it better achieves the end of the art.

scenes.title: The End of the Book
scenes.summary: A last summary of tragedy and epic, their kinds and parts, criticisms and solutions. The discussion of comedy, promised earlier, is lost.
